analysis:
This batch has only changelog fragments and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md. No source code is supplied, so no concrete regression can be cited. The text describes behavior that other passes must check against the code.

Changelog items and relevant threats:
- glm53-native-prerequisites.md, GLM-5.3-Flash coordinator-connected serving: M5 Max/Ultra with at least 256 GB, runtime capability `glm5_next_v1`. A hardware-capability claim is self-reported (TB-002, TB-009, T-055). Also covered: a catalog aggregate/revision receipt binding the loaded bytes (A-004, T-012, T-027); uncached F_NOCACHE hashing before and after load, with digests unchanged; and the 400/503 capacity refusals before response headers.
- glm53-native-prerequisites.md, prefix cache (T-041): the encrypted SSD prefix store is default-on for the pinned GLM identity, with `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` opt-out. It reports typed `detail="<reason>"` on local `/metrics`. A DEBUG-only `DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE` takes a persistent cache key from a file. The claim is that release builds do not contain this path. Reviewers should verify that claim (A-003, T-011, T-041). Image and video rows never reuse cached prefixes.
- glm53-video-input.md (L3): the provider now decodes consumer-supplied inline `data:video/mp4` and `data:video/quicktime`. Decoded frames are capped at 512 MiB and 28,532 visual tokens. This is adversarial-consumer media-parsing attack surface (ADV-002), and T-050 temp-file plaintext is adjacent. The changelog does not say whether temp files are used, so this is unverified.
- local-responses-continuation.md: local-only in-memory retention of prompts, reasoning and tool history via a `previous_response_id` LRU plus a separate object store. This is relevant to A-001 and TB-003 (operator memory access). The docs say it is not persisted and `store:false` suppresses saves.
- mimo-schema-ingress-parity.md and ssd-test-volume-selection.md are test or normalization changes. The SSD change says production cache safeguards are unchanged.

hardware-support.md is documentation: GLM load pricing, wired residency, and retained owners after faults. It records fail-closed behavior (retain roots and publication refusal) but does not by itself change controls.

The threat model may need new entries for GLM video decode and the Responses continuation store. The supplied evidence cannot establish control gaps, so I raise no findings. Verify the code paths named in the changelogs.
